_comment: Golden-corpus regression fixtures for build_dispatch_plan()'s deterministic
selector. Each case is run through build_dispatch_plan() in standalone
mode (Agentic SDLC lifecycle contract forced unavailable, see
test_selection_golden_corpus.py) so the corpus is reproducible without
AGENTIC_SDLC_BIN or network access. 'expected' compares exactly against
the four build_dispatch_plan() output fields named in the requirements
baseline (primary, reviewers, support, matched_routes); 'team_ids' is an
optional fifth field asserted only for cases whose purpose is to pin a
team_recipes trigger. Task strings reused verbatim from
test_selector.py/test_agents_dispatcher.py are noted in 'description' so
this corpus does not silently drift from those regression tests.
A route/keyword edit that changes any of these fields must update this
file in the same reviewable diff (see CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and B-FR-6).
Coverage: this corpus covers every route category defined in
routing.yaml's routes[] array, matching B-FR-5's 'initial corpus covers
every existing route category' requirement. The route id list is not
enumerated here because it drifts every time a route is added, removed,
or renamed -- routing.yaml's routes[] array is the live list;
test_corpus_covers_every_required_route_category in
test_selection_golden_corpus.py is the enforcement, reading routing.yaml
directly rather than any count or enumeration recorded in this comment.
Most single-route fixtures were
authored fresh (not reused from test_selector.py) specifically to
isolate one route per case; where routing.yaml's own paths/keywords
genuinely overlap between two or more routes (e.g. testing and
black-box-testing both list **/*.feature; backend and
database-reliability both list 'postgresql' as a keyword), the fixture
description says so explicitly rather than treating the extra matched
route as an authoring mistake. The corpus also separately pins the
'production' and 'destructive' risk_rules with distinct fixtures
(PRODUCTION-RISK-1, DESTRUCTIVE-RISK-1) since they have separate
keyword_groups, human_gate, and reviewers in routing.yaml and one does
not stand in for the other. A future routing.yaml edit that adds,
removes, or renames a route category must update this comment and the
corresponding fixture(s) in the same diff, and
test_corpus_covers_every_required_route_category in
test_selection_golden_corpus.py enforces that every route id currently
in routing.yaml is represented in this file's matched_routes.
42 fixtures changed their expected 'workflow' in the #210 change that
gave every route in routing.yaml an explicit 'workflow_shape'. Before
it, _select_workflow()'s final stage tested a hardcoded set of four
route ids, so every other route -- all 86 '*-execution' routes among
them -- contributed no shape and fell through to 'unclassified' by
omission rather than by judgment. Each changed expectation carries its
own one-sentence justification in that fixture's 'description', under
the prefix 'Workflow shape:'; none was bulk-rewritten to make the suite
pass. 'unclassified' is still the expectation for 74 fixtures, which is
the point: a route that claims no delivery shape (advisory, assessment,
review, governance, support, documentation, evidence, and the
security-, verify-, and operations-phase execution routes) now declares
'unclassified' deliberately.
11 fixtures changed their expected 'support' in the #223 change that
removed application-engineer from the execution routes carrying a target
project's artifacts. application-engineer's own AGENT.md scopes it to
this suite's own tooling and explicitly directs a target project's
capability work elsewhere, so those routes dispatched an agent as support
on work its role definition tells it to decline -- the same defect #213
fixed for linux-systems-execution, found to be systemic afterwards. Each
changed expectation carries its own justification in that fixture's
'description', under the prefix 'Support staffing (#223):', derived route
by route from the artifact the route matches and from the accountability
the route's own primary names -- never from the shape or from the other
routes' staffing. Ten resolved to backend-engineer and one
(mcp-server-execution) to ai-engineer; that convergence is the catalog's
existing vocabulary, not a bulk replace -- go-service-execution,
python-automation-execution, and node-typescript-execution already staff
backend-engineer for implementers naming that same
backend-engineer-or-application-engineer pair, and
javascript-maintenance-execution already resolves its
'frontend-engineer or application-engineer' pair to frontend-engineer. Two of #223's opening hypotheses did not survive the
derivation and are recorded where they failed: kernel-module-execution
and the other on-device routes are not infrastructure-provisioner work
(the host-platform counterparts linux-systems-execution and
embedded-linux-platform-execution exist separately and already carry it),
and mcp-server-execution is not backend-engineer work (its implementer's
AGENT.md does not offer that role, and the artifact is the model-facing
surface). No workflow shape and no reviewers slot changed; the six
execution routes whose artifacts are this suite's own tooling
(selector-test, agent-workflow, git-operations, dependency-remediation,
shell-automation, supply-chain-remediation) keep application-engineer
deliberately, each confirmed against its primary's AGENT.md.
Four fixtures changed in the #227/#228/#229 follow-up pass, and one was
added. #227: ebpf-execution, kernel-module-execution, and
mcp-server-execution each gained `security-reviewer`, because each
primary's own AGENT.md commits to an independent security handoff its
route staffed nobody to perform. Two of the three name the role
literally, so no alternative was weighed there; ebpf-implementer named
none, so `pipeline-security-reviewer` and `supply-chain-security-reviewer`
were weighed against the artifact and rejected, and that implementer's
prose was tightened to name the role the route now staffs. test-engineer
and code-reviewer stay on all three -- the missing half was security, not
code or test review -- and no support staffing or workflow_shape moved.
The convergence on one role is a per-route result, not a bulk replace:
the catalog carries three security-specific reviewers
(security-reviewer, pipeline-security-reviewer,
supply-chain-security-reviewer) and supply-chain-remediation-execution
keeps a different one of them.
#229: supply-chain-remediation-execution's support moved from
application-engineer to cicd-engineer. Its primary names no
accountability, so the derivation runs from the artifact; #223's reading
of this route as this suite's own tooling does not survive it, since
`security/supply-chain-remediation/**` is a target-project path and this
repository's own supply-chain surface is matched by the separate
`supply-chain` and `packaging` routes. Its reviewers were already correct
and did not change. dependency-remediation-execution shares the shape and
the same objection to application-engineer, but no replacement is
derivable from its own primary, so it was left alone rather than moved on
a guess.
#228: agent-workflow-execution gained `roster/workflows/**` next to its
pre-#84 `agents/workflows/**`. No existing expectation moved, because the
existing fixture matches on keywords; AGENT-WORKFLOW-ROSTER-PATH-1 was
added to pin the path signal, and it is the only fixture added by this
pass.

cases.description: #189 review finding 2 and #196: root pyproject.toml is deliberately NOT a packaging-route path. It is a generic file present in arbitrary downstream Python projects, and routing.yaml ships as the BASE ruleset to every consuming project (routing_overlay.py only lets a consumer widen a base route, never narrow it) -- claiming it under a route named 'packaging' whose keywords are about this repo's own Cline ports and plugin manifests would be wrong for every consumer. A pyproject.toml-only change with no packaging keyword (and no other route's keyword -- the task text deliberately avoids change_intake baseline words like 'update'/'change' and supply-chain's 'dependency' so the result is genuinely needs-triage, not just support-only) is therefore needs-triage, not the packaging route. The distinctive Cadre CLI files VERSION and VERSION route through agent-suite-governance; root pyproject.toml remains intentionally unclaimed.

#196 negative fixture: kernel/pyproject.toml and engine/pyproject.toml remain intentionally unclaimed by path. They carry dependency metadata, but kernel/ and engine/ are ordinary downstream directory names, and the selector cannot yet express a path-and-intent or repository-identity predicate that would avoid non-narrowable base-rule matches for consumers.

#196 negative fixture, completing the CHANGELOG's intentionally-unclaimed list: the kernel module, its validation requirements and dev entrypoint, the engine package, and bin/ stay unclaimed by path for the same base-ruleset reason as the nested pyproject.toml files -- kernel/, engine/, and bin/ are ordinary downstream directory names, and routing_overlay.py lets a consumer widen a base route but never narrow it. Pinned so a future dependency-manifest or supply-chain glob cannot quietly widen into them.
#196 positive fixture: VERSION routes through agent-suite-governance as a distinctive file in this repository's pip distribution package.
#196 positive fixture: VERSION routes through agent-suite-governance as the version file root pyproject.toml reads through [tool.hatch.version].

Covers _select_workflow()'s incident/support exclusion, which two reviewers found reachable but untested: when the frame is incident coordination the label stays support-escalation, while the rollback route's roles are still selected.

architecture-diagram execution route keeps cloud-architect accountable while selecting the specialist; the documentation and architecture-design overlap comes from the diagram's .mmd architecture path. Reviewer staffing -- examined and deliberately NOT changed, recorded so a future sweep does not re-litigate it. The #227-class sweep (a primary's AGENT.md naming a read_only role the route's own `reviewers` does not staff) flags this route for `architecture-authority` and `code-reviewer`, and both are false positives of that heuristic. (1) The naming sentence is not a handoff commitment. Every other primary the sweep flags uses the same unconditional conjunction -- hand off to independent X *and* Y review. `architecture-diagram-author` alone reads "Hand off to an independent `technical-writer`, `code-reviewer`, or `architecture-authority` when architectural claims require review": three alternatives joined by "or", gated on a condition that holds for a subset of diagrams. A route staffs the review a plan always needs; a conditional alternative-set is not that, and staffing all three would dispatch two reviewers the sentence never asks for together. (2) `architecture-authority` is specifically wrong here, and would be wrong even if the sentence were unconditional. Its AGENT.md scopes its Inputs to "The change under review, specifically any code or configuration touching an infrastructure interface" and its finding is "absolute -- a missing boundary element blocks the change unconditionally". A Mermaid or drawio diagram is neither code nor configuration touching an infrastructure interface, and putting a gate-holding authority whose finding is unconditionally blocking into a routine `reviewers` slot would attach a blocking boundary gate to every diagram edit.
